title: Follow-ups from PR #200 review (frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #200 (frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups), tracked here so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: theme.palette.season.spring (#368139) is now perceptually very close to theme.palette.signal.buy (#2e7d32): independently-computed Euclidean RGB distance ~11.4 (down from ~46 for the pre-PR spring value #43a047), because darkening spring's lightness to clear the WCAG 4.5:1 text-contrast floor (per this PR) closed most of the lightness gap that was previously the only thing separating the two -- their hue (~122-123 degrees) and saturation (~41-46%) were already nearly identical before this PR. theme.test.ts's existing 'defines four distinct Indicator Season colors ... none of which reuse a BUY/SELL/HOLD signal color' guard only checks exact hex-string inequality, so it doesn't (and didn't) catch this near-miss. Rendered raw swatches of the two colors side by side are close to visually indistinguishable; in the actual UI the collision is partly mitigated by common/SeasonBadge's outlined-Chip style + icon + the 'Informational -- not a signal' caption versus SignalBadge/the Impulse chip's filled style, but the underlying color values no longer read as clearly distinct on their own. Consider either shifting season.spring's hue slightly away from signal.buy's (not just adjusting lightness) or adding a perceptual-distance (not just exact-inequality) guard to theme.test.ts, then re-verify against signal.buy/sell/hold and the other palette entries.

decisions.decision: Shifted season.spring's hue from pure green (#368139, H~122°, matching signal.buy's H~123°) to yellow-green (#617a2e, H~80°) rather than adjusting lightness/saturation again, while keeping WCAG 4.5:1+ contrast against white. Chose the new hex by binary-searching lightness at H=80°/S=45% for a ~4.85:1 contrast ratio (consistent with the ~4.8:1 margin target the prior PR used for all four season colors), then confirmed via CIE76 Lab ΔE that it clears >=19 ΔE from every other palette color (signal.buy/sell/hold, riskBreach.main, divergence.main, the other three season colors, kangarooTail.main) -- comfortably above the 15 ΔE guard floor this task also adds.
decisions.rationale: The prior fix (frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups) darkened spring's lightness only, preserving its original hue/saturation -- but since spring and signal.buy already shared nearly identical hue/saturation before that fix, a lightness-only change could only ever compress or widen the lightness gap, never create real hue-based separation; that's exactly why it collapsed to ~2.6 CIE76 ΔE (measured fresh in this task) once the lightness gap narrowed for the contrast fix. A hue shift breaks that dependency entirely: yellow-green (H~80°) sits roughly 40° away from buy's green (H~123°) and is far enough from hold's orange (H~27°) and autumn's rust (H~22°) to avoid trading one collision for another, while still reading as a plausible 'fresh spring growth' color (distinct from a pure grass green). Rejected shifting toward teal-green instead (e.g. H~150-170°, closer to divergence.main's H~174°/teal): that direction trades a spring/buy collision risk for a spring/divergence one, and would look less like a distinct 'spring' hue on a chart that also renders divergence markers and kangarooTail markers, since it converges toward the same blue-green family divergence.main already occupies. Verified against the full current palette (not just signal.buy) since a hue shift picked to avoid one collision could unintentionally create another.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Also considered leaving spring's hue alone and instead reducing signal.buy's saturation/hue slightly (the other side of the collision) -- rejected because signal.buy is a load-bearing BUY/SELL/HOLD color used across the whole app (SignalBadge, dashboard, position rows, etc.) per docs/Analyse.md's Triple Screen conventions, so changing it would have far wider blast radius than moving the much newer, narrower-scoped season.spring value, and this task's checklist item was scoped to the season badge collision, not the signal palette.

decisions.decision: While implementing the CIE76 ΔE guard requested for the riskBreach group (among others), discovered that theme.palette.riskBreach.main (#d32f2f) was itself only ~3.9 ΔE76 from theme.palette.signal.sell (#c62828) -- an equally severe, previously-undetected near-collision of the exact same kind as the season.spring/signal.buy one this task was opened for (both colors share hue ~0° and similar saturation; only ~3.9 raw RGB Euclidean units separated them, which the theme.test.ts pre-PR review had judged 'far enough' using a cruder metric). Fixed it in the same pass using the same hue-shift technique: riskBreach.main -> #d52651 (crimson/rose, H~345°), clearing >=20 ΔE76 from signal.sell and every other palette color while keeping >=4.5:1 WCAG contrast against both white and riskBreach.background (#fdecea), and staying visually in the 'red/danger' family rather than drifting toward signal.hold's orange or kangarooTail.main's magenta.
decisions.rationale: The task's instructions explicitly named riskBreach as one of the palette groups the strengthened perceptual-distance guard must cover, alongside signal/season/divergence/kangarooTail. Implementing that guard honestly (a real ΔE threshold, not a threshold quietly tuned to dodge known failures) meant it would legitimately fail on the pre-existing riskBreach/sell collision the moment it was added -- leaving that failing, or hand-picking a threshold too low to catch it (below the ~3.9 ΔE that pair sits at), would defeat the entire purpose of adding a perceptual guard and ship a second, larger reported blocker to the reviewer. Fixing it now, while already deep in this exact investigation and using the exact same vetted technique, was the smaller and more honest change than leaving a newly-added test red or silently weakening it. Confirmed via grep that no test or component hardcodes riskBreach.main's literal hex (all reference `theme.palette.riskBreach.main` symbolically), so this is a safe, isolated value change.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered scoping this task strictly to the single checklist item (season.spring only) and leaving riskBreach.main untouched, filing a further follow-up task instead. Rejected: the task's own instructions explicitly listed riskBreach as one of the groups the new guard must cover, and a guard that's honest enough to catch spring/buy is, by construction, also honest enough to catch sell/riskBreach (they're the same magnitude of collision) -- so 'strengthen the guard for riskBreach' and 'leave the riskBreach/sell collision unfixed' are mutually exclusive asks; deferring the fix to yet another followups task while landing a test that would fail against main's current riskBreach.main would not be a mergeable PR. Considered a lower ΔE threshold (e.g. 5) that would pass the original riskBreach/sell pairing without a color change: rejected because that threshold sits below even the fixed spring/buy pair's target margin and wouldn't meaningfully guard against future near-collisions, undermining the whole point of this task.
decisions.chosen_delta_e_threshold: 15 (MIN_DISTINCT_DELTA_E in theme.test.ts) -- above the ~2.3 single-step JND and the observed 2.6-3.9 ΔE of the two real collisions found, comfortably below the ~17.7 ΔE of the closest pair among colors already treated as intentionally distinct (season.summer vs season.autumn) so no unrelated existing pair is newly flagged.
